claim: ATP is essential for all living cells.
source: ATP is essential for all living cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the fundamental role of ATP in cellular function.

claim: The cytosolic ATP level starts to decrease immediately after the activation of caspase-3.
source: We show that the cytosolic ATP level starts to decrease immediately after the activation of caspase-3, and this process is completed typically within 2 hr.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations using FRET biosensors as described in the manuscript.

claim: The ATP decrease process is completed typically within 2 hr after caspase-3 activation.
source: We show that the cytosolic ATP level starts to decrease immediately after the activation of caspase-3, and this process is completed typically within 2 hr.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The ATP decrease was facilitated by caspase-dependent cleavage of the plasma membrane channel pannexin-1.
source: The ATP decrease was facilitated by caspase-dependent cleavage of the plasma membrane channel pannexin-1, indicating that the intracellular decrease of the apoptotic cell is a 'programmed' process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with PANX1 knockout cells and caspase-resistant PANX1 mutants.

claim: The intracellular ATP decrease of the apoptotic cell is a 'programmed' process.
source: The ATP decrease was facilitated by caspase-dependent cleavage of the plasma membrane channel pannexin-1, indicating that the intracellular decrease of the apoptotic cell is a 'programmed' process.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the finding that ATP decrease depends on caspase-mediated cleavage of PANX1.

claim: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 sustained the ability to produce ATP through glycolysis.
source: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 sustained the ability to produce ATP through glycolysis and to consume ATP, and did not stop wasting glucose much longer period than normal apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that PANX1-KO cells maintain ATP levels longer and respond to glycolysis inhibitors.

claim: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 sustained the ability to consume ATP.
source: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 sustained the ability to produce ATP through glycolysis and to consume ATP, and did not stop wasting glucose much longer period than normal apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that PANX1-KO cells show continued blebbing and respond to metabolic inhibitors.

claim: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 did not stop wasting glucose for a much longer period than normal apoptotic cells.
source: Apoptotic cells deficient of pannexin-1 sustained the ability to produce ATP through glycolysis and to consume ATP, and did not stop wasting glucose much longer period than normal apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by glucose consumption and lactate production measurements in wild-type vs PANX1-KO cells.

claim: Pannexin-1 plays a role in arresting the metabolic activity of dead apoptotic cells.
source: Thus, the pannexin-1 plays a role in arresting the metabolic activity of dead apoptotic cells, most likely through facilitating the loss of intracellular ATP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations of glucose consumption and ATP dynamics.

claim: Pannexin-1 arrests metabolic activity most likely through facilitating the loss of intracellular ATP.
source: Thus, the pannexin-1 plays a role in arresting the metabolic activity of dead apoptotic cells, most likely through facilitating the loss of intracellular ATP.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the correlation between PANX1 activity, ATP loss, and metabolic arrest.

claim: Free energy from ATP hydrolysis is utilized in generating and maintaining the plasma membrane potential.
source: Free energy from ATP that is released upon hydrolysis is utilized in various vital processes including the generation and maintenance of the plasma membrane potential (Kaplan, 2002), remodeling of chromatin (Vignali et al., 2000), locomotion of molecular motors (Vale, 2003), protein degradation (Ciechanover, 1994), and metabolic reactions (Voet and Voet, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kaplan, 2002.

claim: Free energy from ATP hydrolysis is utilized in remodeling of chromatin.
source: Free energy from ATP that is released upon hydrolysis is utilized in various vital processes including the generation and maintenance of the plasma membrane potential (Kaplan, 2002), remodeling of chromatin (Vignali et al., 2000), locomotion of molecular motors (Vale, 2003), protein degradation (Ciechanover, 1994), and metabolic reactions (Voet and Voet, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vignali et al., 2000.

claim: Free energy from ATP hydrolysis is utilized in locomotion of molecular motors.
source: Free energy from ATP that is released upon hydrolysis is utilized in various vital processes including the generation and maintenance of the plasma membrane potential (Kaplan, 2002), remodeling of chromatin (Vignali et al., 2000), locomotion of molecular motors (Vale, 2003), protein degradation (Ciechanover, 1994), and metabolic reactions (Voet and Voet, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vale, 2003.

claim: Free energy from ATP hydrolysis is utilized in protein degradation.
source: Free energy from ATP that is released upon hydrolysis is utilized in various vital processes including the generation and maintenance of the plasma membrane potential (Kaplan, 2002), remodeling of chromatin (Vignali et al., 2000), locomotion of molecular motors (Vale, 2003), protein degradation (Ciechanover, 1994), and metabolic reactions (Voet and Voet, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ciechanover, 1994.

claim: Free energy from ATP hydrolysis is utilized in metabolic reactions.
source: Free energy from ATP that is released upon hydrolysis is utilized in various vital processes including the generation and maintenance of the plasma membrane potential (Kaplan, 2002), remodeling of chromatin (Vignali et al., 2000), locomotion of molecular motors (Vale, 2003), protein degradation (Ciechanover, 1994), and metabolic reactions (Voet and Voet, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Voet and Voet, 2010.

claim: Dead cells contain very little, or even no ATP.
source: On the other hand, dead cells contain very little, or even no ATP.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the metabolic state of dead cells.

claim: Apoptosis is characterized by distinctive morphological changes, such as membrane blebbing, nuclear condensation, and externalization of phosphatidylserine.
source: It is characterized by distinctive morphological changes, such as membrane blebbing, nuclear condensation, and externalization of phosphatidylserine (Elmore, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Elmore, 2007.

claim: Cells die from necrosis rather than apoptosis when intracellular ATP is depleted prior to otherwise apoptotic stimuli.
source: It has been reported that cells die from necrosis rather than apoptosis when intracellular ATP is depleted prior to otherwise apoptotic stimuli (Eguchi et al., 1997; Leist et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eguchi et al., 1997 and Leist et al., 1997.

claim: dATP/ATP is required for the formation of cytochrome c/Apaf-1/procaspase-9 complexes.
source: It has been also reported that dATP/ATP is required for the formation of cytochrome c/Apaf-1/procaspase-9 complexes (Hu et al., 1999; Li et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hu et al., 1999 and Li et al., 1997.

claim: ATP is required for chromatin condensation of apoptotic cells.
source: Moreover, it is suggested that ATP is required for chromatin condensation of apoptotic cells (Kass et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kass et al., 1996.

claim: Apoptosis is considered to be an energy-demanding process, requiring intracellular ATP for the execution of the cell death program.
source: Apoptosis is, thus, considered to be an energy-demanding process, requiring intracellular ATP for the execution of the cell death program.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited literature about ATP requirements in apoptosis.

claim: The original ATeam (AT1.03) was cleaved into its constituent pair of separate fluorescent proteins in apoptotic cells, most probably by activated caspases.
source: Unfortunately, we found that the original ATeam (AT1.03) was cleaved into its constituent pair of separate fluorescent proteins in apoptotic cells, most probably by activated caspases (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The altered ATeam (AT1.03CR with D242N and D339G mutations) was not cleaved inside apoptotic cells.
source: We replaced Asp-242 and Asp-339 of AT1.03, which we predicted were within the target sequences of the caspases, with Asn and Gly, respectively, and found that the altered ATeam was not cleaved inside apoptotic cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The intracellular ATP levels remained almost constant for several hours after apoptotic stimulation.
source: Overall, the intracellular ATP levels remained almost constant for several hours after stimulation.
evidence: This is an observation from the single-cell imaging experiments.

claim: The cytosolic ATP levels in apoptotic cells started to decrease after a variable time interval (typically from 3 to 8 hr after apoptotic stimulation).
source: The cytosolic ATP levels in these cells started to decrease after a variable time interval (typically from 3 to 8 hr after apoptotic stimulation, see Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Once the intracellular ATP levels started to decrease, they were depleted within typically 0.5–2 hr.
source: Once the intracellular ATP levels started to decrease, they were depleted within typically 0.5–2 hr.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the imaging data.

claim: The presence of a pan-caspase inhibitor zVAD-fmk almost completely blocked the cytosolic ATP decrease of anti-FAS-induced apoptotic cells.
source: The presence of a pan-caspase inhibitor zVAD-fmk almost completely blocked the cytosolic ATP decrease of anti-FAS-induced apoptotic cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The ATP decrease induced by apoptotic stimuli is most likely a caspase-dependent process.
source: Thus, the ATP decrease induced by apoptotic stimuli is most likely a caspase-dependent process.
evidence: This is inferred from the zVAD-fmk inhibition experiment.

claim: Intracellular ATP started to decrease after the onset of caspase-3 activation.
source: It was observed that intracellular ATP started to decrease after the onset of caspase-3 activation, also supporting that the ATP decrease of the apoptotic cell is a caspase-dependent process.
evidence: This is observed from dual imaging of ATP and caspase-3 activity.

claim: Decreases in the intracellular ATP levels of PANX1-KO cells after caspase-3 activation were significantly slower than those of wild-type HeLa cells when apoptosis was induced by anti-FAS antibody.
source: Strikingly, decreases in the intracellular ATP levels of PANX1-KO cells after caspase-3 activation were significantly slower than those of wild-type HeLa cells when apoptosis was induced by anti-FAS antibody (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: Knockout of PANX1 apparently has no effect on the ability of the cells to undergo cell death.
source: Knockout of PANX1 apparently has no effect on the ability of the cells to undergo cell death.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments with PANX1-KO cells.

claim: A marked suppression of ATP decrease by knockout of PANX1 was also observed when apoptosis was induced by staurosporine.
source: A marked suppression of ATP decrease by knockout of PANX1 was also observed when apoptosis was induced by staurosporine (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: Knockout of PANX1 also suppressed the decrease in ATP during TRAIL-induced apoptosis of SW480 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells.
source: Moreover, knockout of PANX1 also suppressed the decrease in ATP during TRAIL-induced apoptosis of SW480 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: PANX1 is involved in the facilitation of intracellular ATP decreases during apoptosis in multiple cell types and on various apoptotic stimuli.
source: Thus, PANX1 is involved in the facilitation of intracellular ATP decreases during apoptosis in multiple cell types and on various apoptotic stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments with different cell types and apoptotic stimuli.

claim: The intracellular ATP levels of PANX1-KO cells were almost unchanged in the first 30–60 min after the activation of caspase-3, followed by a gradual ATP decline.
source: Notably, the intracellular ATP levels of PANX1-KO cells were almost unchanged in the first 30–60 min after the activation of caspase-3, followed by a gradual ATP decline (Figure 2C–F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Intracellular ATP concentration transiently and repeatedly re-elevated on the course of the gradual ATP decrease in some populations of the PANX1-KO cells.
source: Single-cell imaging also provided unexpected observations that intracellular ATP concentration transiently and repeatedly re-elevated on the course of the gradual ATP decrease in some populations of the PANX1-KO cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cells overexpressing wild-type PANX1 precipitously lost their intracellular ATP, concomitant with the onset of caspase-3 activation, for both anti-FAS- and staurosporine-induced apoptosis.
source: Cells overexpressing wild-type PANX1 precipitously lost their intracellular ATP, concomitant with the onset of caspase-3 activation, for both anti-FAS- and staurosporine-induced apoptosis (Figure 4A–E), further confirming that the PANX1 channel plays a major role in facilitating intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4A–E.

claim: The intracellular ATP depletion was significantly protracted by the overexpression of PANX1-CR (caspase-resistant mutant).
source: Accordingly, the intracellular ATP depletion was significantly protracted by the overexpression of PANX1-CR (Figure 4F; Figure 4G), clearly indicating that the cleavage of the C-terminal region of PANX1 by caspases is required for the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4F and 4G.

claim: The cleavage of the C-terminal region of PANX1 by caspases is required for the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells.
source: Accordingly, the intracellular ATP depletion was significantly protracted by the overexpression of PANX1-CR (Figure 4F; Figure 4G), clearly indicating that the cleavage of the C-terminal region of PANX1 by caspases is required for the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PANX1-CR overexpression experiment.

claim: The cytosolic ATP level after the onset of caspase-3 activation dropped more quickly in the OXPHOS-dominant condition than in the glycolysis-dependent condition.
source: The cytosolic ATP level after the onset of caspase-3 activation dropped more quickly in the OXPHOS-dominant condition than in the glycolysis-dependent condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), probably because mitochondrial membrane potential ∆Ψm, which is required for mitochondrial ATP regeneration, is almost lost upon activation of caspase-3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and 3.

claim: Mitochondrial membrane potential ∆Ψm is almost lost upon activation of caspase-3.
source: The cytosolic ATP level after the onset of caspase-3 activation dropped more quickly in the OXPHOS-dominant condition than in the glycolysis-dependent condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), probably because mitochondrial membrane potential ∆Ψm, which is required for mitochondrial ATP regeneration, is almost lost upon activation of caspase-3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Knockout of PANX1 also suppressed the decrease in cytosolic ATP levels of OXPHOS-dominant cells.
source: Even in this condition, knockout of PANX1 also suppressed the decrease in cytosolic ATP levels of the cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: PANX1 also promotes the intracellular ATP reduction of OXPHOS-dominant cells.
source: This result indicates that PANX1 also promotes the intracellular ATP reduction of OXPHOS-dominant cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the OXPHOS-dominant culture experiments.

claim: Extracellular AMP suppressed the decrease in intracellular ATP levels of apoptotic cells.
source: We monitored cytosolic ATP dynamics in apoptotic cells in the presence of AMP, ADP, or ATP in the culture medium, and found that extracellular AMP suppressed the decrease in intracellular ATP levels of apoptotic cells, while extracellular ADP and ATP exhibited no or negligible effects (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Extracellular ADP and ATP exhibited no or negligible effects on the decrease in intracellular ATP levels of apoptotic cells.
source: We monitored cytosolic ATP dynamics in apoptotic cells in the presence of AMP, ADP, or ATP in the culture medium, and found that extracellular AMP suppressed the decrease in intracellular ATP levels of apoptotic cells, while extracellular ADP and ATP exhibited no or negligible effects (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells is a result of a reduction in adenosine nucleotide pools inside apoptotic cells, which is caused, at least in part, by the release of AMP from the cells.
source: Thus, it is most likely that the intracellular ATP decrease of apoptotic cells is a result of a reduction in adenosine nucleotide pools inside apoptotic cells, which is caused, at least in part, by the release of AMP from the cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the extracellular AMP suppression experiment.

claim: AMP constitutes a large part of adenine nucleotides released from apoptotic cells.
source: This result is consistent with the previous reports that AMP constitutes a large part of adenine nucleotides released from apoptotic cells (Yamaguchi et al., 2014; Boyd-Tressler et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yamaguchi et al., 2014 and Boyd-Tressler et al., 2014.

claim: The fluctuations in free Mg2+ were significantly suppressed in apoptotic PANX1-KO cells.
source: In contrast, the fluctuations in free Mg2+ were significantly suppressed in apoptotic PANX1-KO cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: PANX1 regulates the dynamics of free Mg2+ in apoptotic cells, likely in part by decreasing ATP concentrations inside cells.
source: Taken together, PANX1 regulates the dynamics of free Mg2+ in apoptotic cells, likely in part by decreasing ATP concentrations inside cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Mg2+ imaging experiments.

claim: No significant difference in the externalized PS was observed between wild-type and PANX1-KO HeLa cells.
source: As a result, no significant difference in the externalized PS was observed between wild-type and PANX1-KO HeLa cells (Figure 6B), suggesting that neither the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP reduction or PANX1 itself does not contribute to the externalization of PS during apoptotic progression.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Neither the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP reduction or PANX1 itself does not contribute to the externalization of PS during apoptotic progression.
source: As a result, no significant difference in the externalized PS was observed between wild-type and PANX1-KO HeLa cells (Figure 6B), suggesting that neither the PANX1-dependent intracellular ATP reduction or PANX1 itself does not contribute to the externalization of PS during apoptotic progression.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of difference in PS externalization between wild-type and PANX1-KO cells.

claim: Treatment with either 2DG or sodium oxamate induced a rapid decrease in intracellular ATP concentration in PANX1-KO apoptotic cells.
source: Treatment with either 2DG or sodium oxamate induced a rapid decrease in intracellular ATP concentration (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Treatment with oligomycin A, an inhibitor of OXPHOS, seemed to have only a small effect on intracellular ATP dynamics under glycolysis-dependent conditions.
source: In contrast, treatment with oligomycin A, an inhibitor of OXPHOS, seemed to have only a small effect on intracellular ATP dynamics under this condition (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Apoptotic processes do not disrupt the glycolytic system of the cells.
source: These observations indicate that apoptotic processes do not disrupt the glycolytic system of the cells and that even dying apoptotic cells retain the ability to regenerate ATP by glycolysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the response of apoptotic PANX1-KO cells to glycolysis inhibitors.

claim: Even dying apoptotic cells retain the ability to regenerate ATP by glycolysis.
source: These observations indicate that apoptotic processes do not disrupt the glycolytic system of the cells and that even dying apoptotic cells retain the ability to regenerate ATP by glycolysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the response of apoptotic PANX1-KO cells to glycolysis inhibitors.

claim: At least some of the intracellular ATP-utilizing systems are active during apoptosis if sufficient intracellular ATP is present.
source: The rapid decrease in cytosolic ATP concentration of apoptotic PANX1-KO cells by inhibition of glycolysis also implies that at least some of the intracellular ATP-utilizing systems are active during apoptosis if sufficient intracellular ATP is present.
evidence: This is inferred from the rapid ATP decrease upon glycolysis inhibition in PANX1-KO cells.

claim: Apoptotic cells treated with a PANX1 inhibitor showed continuous and extensive blebbing.
source: It has been previously reported that apoptotic cells treated with a PANX1 inhibitor showed continuous and extensive blebbing (Poon et al., 2014), which is dependent on myosin ATPase (Coleman et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Poon et al., 2014 and Coleman et al., 2001.

claim: PANX1-KO cells showed more extensive blebbing than wild-type cells during apoptosis.
source: Consistently, we also observed that PANX1-KO cells showed more extensive blebbing than wild-type cells during apoptosis (Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Forced ATP depletion of apoptotic PANX1-KO cells by 2DG leaded to the reduction of the blebbing of the cells.
source: Moreover, forced ATP depletion of apoptotic PANX1-KO cells by 2DG leaded to the reduction of the blebbing of the cells (Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Videos 3 and 4.

claim: Glucose consumption and lactate production by wild-type cells had almost ceased by 16 hr after induction of apoptosis.
source: Glucose consumption and lactate production by wild-type cells had almost ceased by 16 hr after induction of apoptosis, while those by PANX1-KO cells continued for at least 32 hr when apoptosis was induced by anti-FAS (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Glucose consumption and lactate production by PANX1-KO cells continued for at least 32 hr when apoptosis was induced by anti-FAS.
source: Glucose consumption and lactate production by wild-type cells had almost ceased by 16 hr after induction of apoptosis, while those by PANX1-KO cells continued for at least 32 hr when apoptosis was induced by anti-FAS (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Apoptotic cells with deficient PANX1 activity have a prolonged glycolytic activity compared to normal apoptotic cells.
source: Thus, apoptotic cells with deficient PANX1 activity have a prolonged glycolytic activity compared to normal apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the glucose consumption and lactate production measurements.

claim: Activation of PANX1 channels thwarts glucose expenditure of apoptotic cells, most likely by rapidly depleting intracellular ATP reserves.
source: Taken together, activation of PANX1 channels thwarts glucose expenditure of apoptotic cells, most likely by rapidly depleting intracellular ATP reserves (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the glucose consumption and ATP dynamics data.

claim: PANX1 belongs to the innexin/pannexin superfamily and forms a heptameric pore in the plasma membrane.
source: PANX1 belongs to the innexin/pannexin superfamily and forms a heptameric pore in the plasma membrane (Deng et al., 2020; Michalski et al., 2020; Qu et al., 2020), functioning as a large-pore channel capable of passing small molecules (Bao et al., 2004; Dahl and Muller, 2014; Panchin et al., 2000; Penuela et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Deng et al., 2020; Michalski et al., 2020; Qu et al., 2020.

claim: PANX1 functions as a large-pore channel capable of passing small molecules.
source: PANX1 belongs to the innexin/pannexin superfamily and forms a heptameric pore in the plasma membrane (Deng et al., 2020; Michalski et al., 2020; Qu et al., 2020), functioning as a large-pore channel capable of passing small molecules (Bao et al., 2004; Dahl and Muller, 2014; Panchin et al., 2000; Penuela et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bao et al., 2004; Dahl and Muller, 2014; Panchin et al., 2000; Penuela et al., 2013.

claim: Apoptotic cells release ATP, AMP, and also UTP through the PANX1 channel as 'find-me' signals to attract macrophages.
source: It has been reported that apoptotic cells release ATP, AMP, and also UTP through the PANX1 channel as 'find-me' signals to attract macrophages and that the PANX1 channel is opened by caspase-3/7, which cleaves the C-terminal region of the channel (Chekeni et al., 2010; Elliott et al., 2009; Yamaguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chekeni et al., 2010; Elliott et al., 2009; Yamaguchi et al., 2014.

claim: The PANX1 channel is opened by caspase-3/7, which cleaves the C-terminal region of the channel.
source: It has been reported that apoptotic cells release ATP, AMP, and also UTP through the PANX1 channel as 'find-me' signals to attract macrophages and that the PANX1 channel is opened by caspase-3/7, which cleaves the C-terminal region of the channel (Chekeni et al., 2010; Elliott et al., 2009; Yamaguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chekeni et al., 2010; Elliott et al., 2009; Yamaguchi et al., 2014.

claim: Accumulation of extracellular adenine nucleotides correlates with decreases in intracellular ATP during the apoptotic progression of Jurkat cells.
source: The previous cell population-based study has reported that accumulation of extracellular adenine nucleotides correlates with decreases in intracellular ATP during the apoptotic progression of Jurkat cells (Boyd-Tressler et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Boyd-Tressler et al., 2014.

claim: The suppression of glucose expenditure by apoptotic cells may benefit surrounding live cells because the resource of glucose for surrounding live cells would be limited if dying cells continued to consume glucose.
source: The suppression of glucose expenditure by apoptotic cells may benefit surrounding live cells because the resource of glucose for surrounding live cells would be limited if dying cells continued to consume glucose.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the biological significance of PANX1-mediated metabolic arrest.

claim: Macrophages that eat apoptotic cells may encounter a risk of energy deprivation if the eaten cells actively consume glucose inside the macrophages.
source: Besides, macrophages that eat apoptotic cells may encounter a risk of energy deprivation if the eaten cells actively consume glucose inside the macrophages.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the biological significance of PANX1-mediated metabolic arrest.

claim: The removal of apoptotic cells by macrophages is critical to suppress inflammation and autoimmune diseases.
source: Because the removal of apoptotic cells by macrophages is critical to suppress inflammation and autoimmune diseases (Nagata, 2018), stimulating local macrophages by ATP and related nucleotides released through PANX1 channels should be a biologically important process in apoptosis (Chekeni et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nagata, 2018.

claim: Stimulating local macrophages by ATP and related nucleotides released through PANX1 channels should be a biologically important process in apoptosis.
source: Because the removal of apoptotic cells by macrophages is critical to suppress inflammation and autoimmune diseases (Nagata, 2018), stimulating local macrophages by ATP and related nucleotides released through PANX1 channels should be a biologically important process in apoptosis (Chekeni et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chekeni et al., 2010.

claim: Cells in normal adult tissues preferentially use oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in mitochondria for the regeneration of ATP.
source: It is known that cells in normal adult tissues preferentially use oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in mitochondria for the regeneration of ATP, while cells in embryonic tissues and tumors use glycolysis (Vander Heiden et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vander Heiden et al., 2009.

claim: Cells in embryonic tissues and tumors use glycolysis for ATP regeneration.
source: It is known that cells in normal adult tissues preferentially use oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in mitochondria for the regeneration of ATP, while cells in embryonic tissues and tumors use glycolysis (Vander Heiden et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vander Heiden et al., 2009.

claim: Most of the intracellular ATP form a complex with Mg2+, due to the high affinity of ATP for Mg2+.
source: It is known that most of the intracellular ATP form a complex with Mg2+, due to the high affinity of ATP for Mg2+ (Gupta and Moore, 1980; Grubbs, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gupta and Moore, 1980 and Grubbs, 2002.

claim: ATP acts as a major intracellular chelator for Mg2+.
source: Thus, ATP acts as a major intracellular chelator for Mg2+.
evidence: This is inferred from the high affinity of ATP for Mg2+.

claim: Externalized PS functions as an 'eat-me' signal for phagocytosis of apoptotic cells by macrophages.
source: Externalized PS functions as an 'eat-me' signal for phagocytosis of apoptotic cells by macrophages.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about PS externalization in apoptosis.

claim: Mg2+ is an essential divalent cation in cells, required for various cellular processes, including the activity of endonucleases and the compaction of chromosomes during cell division.
source: Mg2+ is an essential divalent cation in cells, required for various cellular processes, including the activity of endonucleases and the compaction of chromosomes during cell division (Hartwig, 2001; Maeshima et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hartwig, 2001 and Maeshima et al., 2018.

claim: Membrane blebbing is dependent on myosin ATPase.
source: It has been previously reported that apoptotic cells treated with a PANX1 inhibitor showed continuous and extensive blebbing (Poon et al., 2014), which is dependent on myosin ATPase (Coleman et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Coleman et al., 2001.

claim: In pyroptosis, gasdermin-D has been reported to form pores as large as 10 nm in diameter in the plasma membrane and to release adenine nucleotides.
source: In pyroptosis, gasdermin-D has been reported to form pores as large as 10 nm in diameter in the plasma membrane and to release adenine nucleotides (Liu et al., 2016; Russo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2016 and Russo et al., 2016.

claim: The overexpression of PANX1-CR significantly suppresses the release of ATP from apoptotic cells.
source: In fact, it has been reported that the overexpression of PANX1-CR significantly suppresses the release of ATP from apoptotic cells (Chekeni et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chekeni et al., 2010.

claim: Apoptosis progresses differently between cells, even those cultured and stimulated in identical conditions.
source: Because apoptosis progresses differently between cells (for example see Goldstein et al., 2000), even those cultured and stimulated in identical conditions, it has been quite difficult to precisely understand the dynamics of the intracellular ATP level in each dying apoptotic cell, and difficult to tell whether the ATP decrease accompanies specific apoptotic events.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Goldstein et al., 2000.

claim: mKOκ-mKate2 FRET pair is compatible with CFP-YFP FRET pair because they use different spectral windows.
source: It was recently demonstrated that mKOκ-mKate2 FRET pair is compatible with CFP-YFP FRET pair because they use different spectral windows (Watabe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Watabe et al., 2020.

claim: It is possible to use both biosensors to fluorescently image ATP level and caspase-3 activity in the same apoptotic cell.
source: Thus, it is possible to use both biosensors to fluorescently image ATP level and caspase-3 activity in the same apoptotic cell (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the dual imaging experiments shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: In wild-type cells, free Mg2+ was transiently decreased after shrinkage of the cells.
source: In wild-type cells, free Mg2+ was transiently decreased after shrinkage of the cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the Mg2+ imaging experiments.

claim: Both wild-type and PANX1-KO cells exhibited similar glucose consumption and lactate production rates when apoptosis was not induced.
source: Both cells exhibited similar glucose consumption and lactate production rates when apoptosis was not induced (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 7E.
